turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Hale, got your vitals while you were waiting. Blood pressure is one forty-eight over ninety-two, pulse seventy-eight, and your temp is thirty-six point eight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, alright. Can we just get this over with? My foot is killing me and I barely slept.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor's finishing up next door. Keep that foot up on the stool if you can.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr. Hale, Dr. Pell. What happened with the foot?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Big toe. The right one. Swelled up and it hurts like hell. Started last night.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Zero to ten, the pain?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, an eight? Nine when I put weight on it. I'm exhausted.
[SEG0008] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He was up most of the night with it. I'm June, I come help him at the house three days a week.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which toe, the big one?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I already said the toe. And the beer doesn't help me sleep either, weekends are a mess.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Big toe, yes or no?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Right big toe. Can you not make me repeat everything?
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any injury?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I didn't hit it or anything.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Red? Hot to the touch?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): It's red, yeah, and puffy. Hot, I guess.
[SEG0017] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He wouldn't even let me get a sock on it this morning.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever? Chills?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. I'm just wiped out, that's all.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Happened before?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Same thing about a year back. Went away after a few days. I didn't bother coming in.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicines?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): A water pill. For my blood pressure. Every morning.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Name and the dose?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, the little white tablet. Hydrochloro-something. Twenty-five milligrams.
[SEG0026] person_4 (CAREGIVER): It's hydrochlorothiazide, twenty-five. I set it out with his breakfast.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't like taking a bunch of pills.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): How much do you drink?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, the toe was fine yesterday afternoon. I was walking around the kitchen, no problem.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alcohol. Beer, wine, or liquor, and how much?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Beer. Weekends. Saturday and Sunday, usually three or four cans. Not during the week.
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): That's about right. I don't see him drink on the weekdays I'm there.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Kick or stub anything?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I said no. Wait. Well, actually, last night I did kick the chair leg. Stubbed that same toe. Wasn't that hard. I forgot.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stubbed it, then it swelled.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Hurt right away, then overnight it blew up. Now I can barely touch it.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right first toe is swollen, red over the joint, very tender. Skin's intact. No cut, no pus.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't press on it. Jesus. I'm too tired for this.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not pressing hard. Pulses in the foot feel fine. No streaking up the foot.
[SEG0043] person_4 (CAREGIVER): You think it's broken?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Could be a gout flare, could be inflammation from stubbing it, could be an early infection. I'm not calling it one thing yet.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Gout? My dad had that. I don't want gout.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted about your father. That doesn't settle it. I won't conclude gout off one look.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): So what are you doing? I need something for this pain. I'm miserable.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Blood uric acid today. It won't prove the cause by itself. I still want the number.
[SEG0049] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Should he stop the water pill? I read those can stir this up.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't stop it on your own. Keep the hydrochlorothiazide, twenty-five milligrams, every morning.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine, I won't stop the pill. And the pain? Hello?

[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Starting colchicine. One point two milligrams now, two of the point six tablets, then point six milligrams one hour later. After that, point six once a day for a few days.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Not ibuprofen? I've got that at home.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): I could have used an NSAID, naproxen, but with the thiazide I'd rather not until kidney numbers are in. Colchicine is the plan.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Whatever. My stomach's already sour from no breakfast.
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the colchicine gives you bad diarrhea, stop it and call. Don't add ibuprofen on top.
[SEG0057] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll keep an eye out for that.

[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Elevate the foot. Ice in a towel, twenty minutes at a time. Stay off it today, and come back sooner if the redness spreads or you get a fever. Cut the weekend beer down, none while this is hot if you can.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah I'll keep it up and ice it. If the pill gives me the runs I'll call you. Beer, I'll try, no promises.
[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nurse will send you for that uric acid draw before you leave. I'll see you back in one week.
[SEG0061] person_1 (NURSE): I'll walk you down to the lab once you're done here. It's just around the corner.
